meta.keys: grid square ids from grid.geojson (farmland squares only)
meta.low_typical_high: 10th percentile, median and 90th percentile of the seasons 2001-2020
meta.season: named by harvest year: season 2024 = September 2023 to August 2024
meta.pixels: MODIS pixels that are at least half rain-fed arable land (WorldCover cropland and CORINE 211), good quality only

peak_day.what: day of the peak, counted from 1 September

greenup_day.what: day greenness rises past halfway to the peak, counted from 1 September (found between 16-day composites)

dryoff_day.what: day greenness falls back below halfway, counted from 1 September (found between 16-day composites; early = crop finished early)

bare_months.what: months per season with average greenness below 0.3

peak_by_season.shape: one value per season in meta.seasons

dryoff_by_season.shape: one value per season in meta.seasons

modis_ndvi.name: MODIS Terra Vegetation Indices 16-day 250 m (MOD13Q1 v6.1)
modis_ndvi.licence: NASA data: no restrictions on use
modis_ndvi.cite: Didan, K. (2021). MOD13Q1 MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061. NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061

hls.name: Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLSL30 and HLSS30 v2.0)
hls.licence: NASA data: no restrictions on use
hls.cite: Masek, J. et al. (2021). HLS Operational Land Surface Reflectance and TOA Brightness Daily Global 30m v2.0. NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/HLS/HLSL30.002, doi:10.5067/HLS/HLSS30.002

sentinel2.name: Sentinel-2 surface reflectance (harmonised) with Cloud Score+
sentinel2.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data: free, full and open; Cloud Score+ CC BY 4.0
sentinel2.cite: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (ESA). Pasquarella, V. J. et al. (2023). Cloud Score+. CVPR Workshops

worldcover.name: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200
worldcover.cite: Zanaga, D. et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7254221

corine.name: CORINE Land Cover 2018
corine.licence: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service: free, full and open access, with attribution
corine.cite: European Union, Copernicus Land Monitoring Service 2018, European Environment Agency (EEA)

meta.ai_assistance: Produced by notebooks written with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) and run by the Field Shift team in Google Colab with Google Earth Engine. Data values come from the cited datasets and were not written by the AI, except a few published values from the trial at the demo field (its station's rain and temperature, and its soil description), which were copied by hand from Denora et al. (2025) and are labelled as such.
